paragraphs: Overall credibility check result for this report: not passed. For step s_combo1 (static, combination combo1), the reaction balance check passed, which means the applied loads and support reactions cancel each other.

The maximum von Mises stress, away from constrained faces, is {{s_combo1.vm_max_mpa}}, against a material yield strength of {{s_combo1.strength_mpa}}. However, the mesh convergence check on maximum stress did not pass. The peak stress rose with each refinement, from {{s_combo1.conv2.level0}} on the first mesh to {{s_combo1.conv2.level1}} on the second and {{s_combo1.conv2.level2}} on the third. This pattern points to a suspected stress singularity, such as a sharp corner or a point load. The stress at that location should not be used as a design basis, and the reported maximum stress should not be regarded as converged or reliable.

The maximum displacement of {{s_combo1.u_max_mm}} did converge. Its values were {{s_combo1.conv3.level0}}, {{s_combo1.conv3.level1}} and {{s_combo1.conv3.level2}} across the three meshes, and the convergence check on displacement passed. This only concerns global displacement and says nothing about local stress.

The mesh quality check is unknown. Second-order elements on curved surfaces were too distorted after order elevation, so straight-edged second-order elements were used, with curved surfaces approximated by chords. Stresses near curved surfaces may therefore deviate noticeably.
No safety factor is given, because the credibility checks did not pass (overall result: not passed).

Limitations: the analysis is linear elastic with small deformation, with no contact, residual stress or surface hardening. Stresses near constrained and loaded faces come from idealized boundary conditions and were excluded from the maximum stress evaluation. Stress at sharp corners grows with mesh refinement (a theoretical singularity), so it is not suitable as a direct design basis.
suggestions: Locate the position of the maximum stress in the third mesh and have an engineer check whether it is a sharp corner or a point load.
If the feature is a sharp corner, model the real fillet radius there, or apply the load over a realistic area instead of at a point, then rerun the convergence study.
Refine the mesh on curved surfaces so that there are several element layers across the curvature, and use curved second-order elements if the geometry allows.
Evaluate stress at the singular location with a method that does not depend on the peak value, such as the stress at a set distance from the corner, and confirm it with the engineer.
Rerun the credibility checks after remeshing, and only consider a safety factor once all checks have passed.
